segments.title: 1997 vs 2026: THE T05 OPENING
segments.credit: Original footage: Local Ditch Gaming, youtube.com/@LocalDitchGaming, used with permission
segments.caption: The mission's own fly-in, 1997 game on the left (not tick-locked: lined up by eye on the cut to the cockpit)\N600 m and coarse terrain   vs   2300 m, full-detail cliffs, morphing terrain

segments.title: SAME ROUTE. SAME CAR. SAME 1997 TICK.
segments.caption: Both sides start on the first moment the car moves; the MPH counters agree because the sim is the 1997 one\N{\fs28}counters = each recording's own telemetry (screen capture costs ~25 % of the frame rate)

segments.title: SMOOTHNESS: 20 FPS vs THE TICK, DRAWN AT DISPLAY RATE
segments.caption: A fast weave at half speed: the same 41.667 ms physics step, every display frame in between interpolated

segments.title: THE JUMP, AS IN 1997
segments.caption: Canyon ramp: take-off 49.9 vs 50.0 m/s, apex 10.0 m as retail; the nose-dive off the lip eased 9 %

segments.title: THE FAR EDGE FADES INTO THE SKY
segments.caption: The last 25 % of the 2300 m view feathers to transparent instead of a hard wall (zoomed, half speed)

segments.title: TERRAIN THAT MORPHS INSTEAD OF POPPING
segments.caption: Level-of-detail splits blend in over 25 % of their ring; shading steps 16 -> 32-40 grey levels (zoomed, half speed)

segments.title: NO POP, LONG VIEW
segments.caption: Owner's drive through the canyon: terrain morphs in and the far edge stays soft at 2300 m

segments.title: LOOK AROUND WHILE YOU DRIVE
segments.caption: Glance left, right and back (keys, pad or opentrack head tracking) - same drive, same moment

segments.title: HEAD TRACKING
segments.caption: opentrack head look (camera at 30 fps): look into the corner, check the mirror - a held glance key still wins

segments.title: A REAR MIRROR THAT SEES
